speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your post-operative check-up. You mentioned occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings; can you tell me exactly when this pain occurs and what specific activities trigger it?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Nerve Entrapment (specifically Great Auricular or Auriculotemporal nerve entrapment) resulting in post-tympanoplasty neuralgia and implant malposition intolerance.

The sharp pain when eating suggests mandibular involvement affecting the auriculotemporal nerve, while the discomfort with earrings points to sensory hyperesthesia or a low-lying skin flap. I have noted your history of recurrent otitis media; does the pain radiate specifically to the angle of the jaw or the temple?
